title: What is known about 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_1LB1RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_1LB1RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the rightward pass over any dense block and the halting situations (kernel), and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps.

What it does. The head sweeps the whole tape. At the left end the tape is dense: blocks of 1s, almost all of length 4j+3, separated by single 0s. The rightward pass rewrites every block 14j+3 0 as the sparse word (1010)j 1000 of the same length. The leftward trip rebuilds dense blocks, but not the same ones: the list of lengths is scrambled each time, and a few cells are added at each end. It shares states A, B and C, and so this rightward pass, with its neighbour 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LB_1LF0LC_1LB1RE.
Where a halt would come from. Only A reading a 1 halts, which happens exactly after A>0 1 or 1 B>1. In 2·108 steps A always reads a 0.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: A with 0 under the head, 1 right; F with 1 two left, 1 left, 0 under the head. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 36,584 cells have been visited and 30,303 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: C crosses a dense block 14n+3 0 in 8n+6 steps and leaves the sparse word (1010)n 1000, for every n; two 1s cost four steps. Seen from B the same pass turns each 0111 into 0100.

claims.title: The halting situations
claims.text: A>0 1 halts after two steps and 1 B>1 after one.

claims.title: Dense and sparse forms
claims.text: At the 1,907 left-end visits of the first 5·10<sup>6</sup> steps, 303,706 of the 306,037 blocks of 1s strictly inside the tape have length 4j+3; at the 660 right-end visits every 1 stands alone (the sparse words), with 32 exceptions.

claims.title: A never reads a 1 in 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps
claims.text: In the first 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps the machine is in state A 23,410,519 times, every time on a 0: the halting transition A1 is never close to firing in a way the run shows.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 7 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 16, p = 6 up to width 16. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..8; n = 9 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The list of block lengths changes from trip to trip like the cells of a cellular automaton; no invariant that rules out A>0 1 and 1 B>1 is known.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RA_1RC0RE_1RD1LB_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1LE_0LC0RF_1RD0LB_1RE1RD_1RA0RC_1LB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine shuttles its tape between two encodings, dense at the left end and sparse at the right end, and scrambles it a little on every trip. This page runs it in your browser and explains the two encodings.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 36,584 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Two encodings of one list
html: Run the simulator and look at the tape each time the head turns at an end. At the left end it is dense: runs of 1s separated by single 0s, nearly all of length 3, 7, 11, 15, … (4j+3). At the right end it is sparse: a string of the four-cell words 0101 and 0001.
The rightward pass is a plain translation. State C walks right and rewrites each dense block two cells at a time; the block 17 0 (j = 1) becomes 1010 1000:

Lean proves this for every j (pass_block in lean/Rules.lean): the number j is kept, only the encoding changes. The leftward trip is a slow zig-zag that turns the sparse words back into dense blocks, and that is where the list is scrambled.

sections.heading: A must read a 1
html: The only missing instruction is A reading a 1. Two local situations lead to it:

A> 0 1      (A on a 0, a 1 to its right)
1 B> 1      (B reads the 1, writes 0, steps back onto the 1 in state A: halt)
and 1 B>1, which halts on the next step. A is entered 23 million times in the first 2·108 steps, always on a 0.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).
After 109 steps the tape spans 36,584 cells (20,105 left of the start, 6,818 right), with a density of 1s of 0.828.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RA_1RC0RE_1RD1LB_0LE0RF_1RA0LD_1LD---: rename A→F, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→C and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB1LE_0LC0RF_1RD0LB_1RE1RD_1RA0RC_1LB---: rename A→F, B→B, C→C, D→D, E→E, F→A and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state F, in a mirror

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LB_1LF0LC_1LB1RE: 9,588,057 configurations, the last at step 9,588,056 here and step 10,000,000 there

summary: Sweeps between a dense form (blocks 1<sup>4j+3</sup> separated by single 0s) at the left end and a sparse form (words 0101, 0001) at the right end; the list of blocks is scrambled on every round trip. Open.
family: two-sided bouncer, dense/sparse translator with chaotic content
